transcript: Whenever any kind of artist dies, and particularly when they die really young, I feel like there is always this sense of, I wish we could have just gotten a little bit more. And unfortunately, most of the time, we never really get any closure on that. And that is what makes the Jonathan Larson Project, a new song cycle that just started performances off Broadway, so special. Because Jonathan Larson tragically passed away at the age of 35, right before rent was scheduled to start previews off Broadway. That musical went on to define a generation. And Jonathan never lived to see any of that success. And rent is still the only full musical we ever got from him. We did eventually get Tick Tick Boom, which was adapted from a solo show that Jonathan did pre rent. But outside of those two shows, it seemed like we were never gonna get any more Jonathan Larson music. But now, miraculously, we have the Jonathan Larson Project, which digs through the archives and his unreleased music to put together a full musical review of all new Jonathan Larson music. None of these songs are from rent or Tick Tick Boom. These are all brand new Jonathan Larson songs that you have not heard before unless you listen to the album version. And even then, there are some songs in this you haven't heard before. Being able to experience new Jonathan Larson music outside of rent and Tick Tick Boom is An experience that, quite frankly, I never thought I would have. And these don't feel like songs that were cut for a reason, either. These are all really great, and I would put it on par with his work in rent and Tick Tick Boom. And despite being written 30+ years ago, so much of the music in this show feels so relevant to a 2025 audience. It really does highlight just how talented Jonathan was and the universality of a lot of his music. And so I really cannot recommend the show enough, not just to Jonathan Larson and rent fans, but really theater fans in general. This truly historic piece of theater is a brilliant tribute to Jonathan Larson and a massive gift to theater kids everywhere.
